strengths: The paper tackles a real bottleneck in 3DGS—iterative densification creates a long optimization path. Replacing it with dense initialization from triangulated 2D correspondences is simple, practical, and aligns with the observed need for faster convergence.

The empirical study is broad: three datasets, multiple quality- and efficiency-focused baselines, per-scene results, qualitative comparisons, and ablations on matching algorithm, noise robustness, densification, hyperparameters, and Gaussian motion.

The method is evaluated with initialization cost included in timing, and it often reduces training time and final Gaussian count while improving LPIPS/SSIM, making the efficiency/quality trade-off compelling.
The approach is orthogonal to existing 3DGS accelerations. Combining it with Taming-3DGS yields consistent gains, showing practical value beyond a single pipeline.

The paper provides useful analysis of why initialization helps: Fig. 5 shows much smaller Gaussian displacement and path length, and Fig. A5 shows dense initialization is pruned to fewer final splats.
Reproducibility details are mostly clear: 3DGS base code, densification disabled, A100 hardware, matching network (RoMa), hyperparameters, and per-scene numbers are reported.
weaknesses: Technical novelty is limited: dense matching, triangulation, and point-cloud initialization are standard MVS components. The contribution is mostly empirical rather than a fundamentally new representation or optimization.

Some claims are overstated. The abstract says the method outperforms quality-focused state-of-the-art and uses half the splats, but on Mip-NeRF360 the 3DGS variant lags 3DGS-MCMC in PSNR/SSIM, and Gaussian reductions are dataset-dependent; the strongest gains often rely on Taming-3DGS integration.

Triangulation is pairwise and lacks explicit multi-view fusion or robust outlier rejection. The paper admits the initialization is noisy and relies on optimization/pruning to clean it up, but does not quantify outlier rates or coverage failures.

The method depends on dense multi-view overlap and many reference views (180 cameras, 15000 keypoints per frame). Sparse-view or undercovered-region performance is not thoroughly evaluated, limiting generality.

A natural baseline is missing: initializing 3DGS from a COLMAP dense/MVS point cloud with densification disabled. Without it, it is unclear how much gain comes from the specific RoMa matching versus dense MVS initialization generally.

The triangulation equations are imprecise as written: Eqs. (5)–(7) form a homogeneous system, but the least-squares form with b=0 would yield a trivial solution if taken literally; the normalization/dimension handling needs clarification.

Some implementation details are inconsistent or incomplete: the main text describes multiple neighboring views per reference image, while the supplement says only the top-1 nearest neighbor is selected; the pruning/opacity-reset schedule when densification is disabled is also not fully described despite Fig. A5 showing a decreasing Gaussian count.
